title: Allocator spiral from tenant-affinity spillover causing cross-env OOMs and KV tombstone corruption
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Production escalation: multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private experienced GPU OOM cascades over a 72-hour window. The cascade correlated with a tenant-affinity change during autoscaling which caused a burst of session handoffs. During the handoffs a concurrent tombstone sweep in the KV index raced with session eviction, producing stale pointers that prevented arenas from reclaiming memory. The allocator entered an "allocation spiral" where new allocations fragmented memory, drove up device-visible resident set, and triggered OOMs on affected GPU nodes. Symptoms: elevated allocation failure rates, sudden latency spikes, repeated model restarts and degraded throughput for small-sequence workloads. We have a P0 customer impact and several enterprise tenants reported timeouts and failed jobs.
root_cause: Race between KV tombstone compaction and session handoff (tenant affinity shift) left orphaned tombstone entries referencing freed KV handles. These orphaned entries prevented slab/arena coalescing. On GPUs with higher device memory pressure, allocator fallback paths fragmented hot arenas leading to OOMs. Secondary factor: recent change to the autoscaler that batches handoffs to reduce churn increased concurrency pressure and widened the window for the race.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix v1: temporarily disable tombstone compaction for sessions being handed off (hosted rollout completed 2025-11-06)
Hotfix v2: conservative autoscaler tweak to stagger handoffs and reduce simultaneous session movement (dedicated rollout staged 2025-11-07)
Customer workaround: reduced per-tenant parallelism and pinned affected tenants to older model-variant to reduce KV churn
investigation_steps: Collected perf traces and GPU resident set samples from affected nodes (N=12 hosts)
Point-in-time heap snapshots of runtime arenas + KV index before/after handoff window
Replayed tenant handoff sequence in testbed with address sanitizer and custom KV instrumentation
Added additional logging and tombstone checksum verification to detect orphaned pointers
proposed_fix: Introduce an eager tombstone-ownership transfer during session handoff: when a session moves, its KV tombstones are atomically re-parented to the destination session before the source frees any handles. In addition, add a lightweight tombstone validation pass in the allocator free path to avoid stale pointer retention. This requires a small runtime API change (kv_reparent_atomic) and a kernel-level allocator reclaim shim to allow fast coalescing.
rollout_plan: Submit patch and land unit + integration tests (CI: kv-reparent + allocator validation)
Canary rollout: 5% of hosted traffic for 24h with enhanced diagnostics
Staged expansion to Dedicated: low-risk nodes first for 48h then full pool
Private customers: publish advisory and backport patch to private bundle; offer on-site upgrade assistance
Post-rollout: monitor OOM rate, allocation latency, KV tombstone checksum errors, per-tenant tail latency
tests_and_checks: New unit tests for kv_reparent_atomic semantics
Stress harness reproducer that runs 1k handoffs/min and verifies no orphaned tombstones
GPU memory soak test for 72h to validate allocation churn profile
Invariant checker in runtime that asserts tombstone->handle pointer validity
